result.summary: This PR makes ScriptCompression::Unser throw std::ios_base::failure when DecompressScript fails, instead of silently leaving the script empty. It adds unit test coverage confirming the throw behavior for an off-curve P2PK, and a new test verifying that a P2PK with a valid X but wrong Y (also unspendable) is stored raw rather than compressed, since compressing it would recompute a valid Y on decompression and make the previously-unspendable output spendable. The fuzz harness for script (de)compression is also strengthened to assert that any successful decompression round-trips back to the same compressed record.
result.problem: ScriptCompression::Unser ignores DecompressScript's return value, so if a compressed script record can't be decompressed (currently only possible via corruption), the resulting script is silently empty, which is consensus-wise anyone-can-spend instead of the intended unspendable off-curve P2PK. This is a latent chainstate-integrity hazard rather than a currently exploitable bug.

result.card: This PR changes ScriptCompression::Unser to throw std::ios_base::failure when a compressed script cannot be decompressed, instead of silently leaving the script empty, which today is equivalent to anyone-can-spend. The author states the worst case is an unspendable off-curve P2PK becoming spendable after corruption, and adds unit and fuzz coverage for that scenario plus a related wrong-Y P2PK case. The bug is currently reachable only through data corruption, not normal validation, so this is a defensive integrity fix rather than an active exploit. One reviewer (sedited) gave an Approach ACK with no stated objections, and the PR is small, fresh, and appears ready for review with nothing pending. No dependencies or blocking issues are noted.
